claim_text: In the same study, lapatinib, trastuzumab, or MEK inhibition prevented ERK activation, while adding HER2 or MEK blockade increased growth inhibition and apoptosis; in BT474-Tr xenografts, trastuzumab plus BEZ235 and AZD6244 plus BEZ235 improved tumor control compared with PI3K-pathway inhibition alone, although BEZ235 plus lapatinib caused unacceptable toxicity in the mouse schedule tested `pmid-21278786`.
evidence_summary: BT474/MCF7-HER2/SKBR3 and BT474-Tr xenograft data show BEZ235-induced ERK phosphorylation was prevented by lapatinib, trastuzumab, or AZD6244; combinations improved proliferation/apoptosis endpoints, trastuzumab+BEZ235 improved xenograft inhibition, AZD6244+BEZ235 improved antitumor activity, and BEZ235+lapatinib caused weight loss/dehydration/lethargy in mice.
reviewer_notes: Claim is specific to HER2-overexpressing preclinical models and older PI3K/mTOR inhibitors, which the text states.

claim_text: Recurrent tumor transplants with Her2/Her3 and MAPK activation were not controlled by pictilisib alone, whereas combined lapatinib plus MEK162 nearly abolished phospho-ERK and produced sustained regression with increased antiproliferative and proapoptotic markers `pmid-26640141`.
evidence_summary: Recurrent NIC+PIK3CAH1047R tumor transplants with aberrant Her2/Her3 and Mapk signaling did not respond to GDC-0941/pictilisib; lapatinib plus MEK162 diminished phospho-ERK, produced sustained tumor regression, and increased antiproliferative and proapoptotic activity.
reviewer_notes: Evidence is from genetic PIK3CA deinduction/recurrent transplant models, not clinical alpelisib resistance.

claim_text: PTEN loss alone did not induce resistance, but it enhanced EGFR-ligand-mediated resistance; PI3K plus MEK, ERK, or EGFR inhibition improved control in resistant cells and xenografts `pmid-25053989`.
evidence_summary: SW48/SW48 H1047R colorectal models showed PTEN knockdown/loss alone did not change GDC-0941 sensitivity, but PTEN-null cells were more resistant with EGFR ligands; resistant cells secreted AREG and EGFR/MAPK cotargeting restored sensitivity or xenograft control when PI3K inhibitor was retained.
reviewer_notes: Paper concerns pan-PI3K pictilisib/GDC-0941 in colorectal models.

claim_text: In KRAS-active NSCLC and HNSCC models, PI-103 produced short-term Akt suppression but 24-hour exposure allowed ERK2-dependent Akt reactivation, and MEK inhibition or ERK2 knockdown restored deeper pathway suppression and improved clonogenic inhibition `pmid-24351425`.
evidence_summary: KRAS-mutant NSCLC and KRAS-overexpressing HNSCC cell lines had Akt suppression after 2 h PI-103 but Akt reactivation after 24 h; PD98059 or ERK2 siRNA blocked reactivation, and PI-103 plus MEK inhibition significantly increased anticlonogenic activity versus PI-103 alone.
reviewer_notes: Preclinical cell-line evidence with PI-103, not PI3K-alpha-selective or breast cancer.

claim_text: Breast cancer RTK-profiling work adds a cautionary pharmacodynamic layer: alpelisib inhibited both AKT and ERK in some PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer cells, but EGFR, HER3, c-MET, FGFR, or RAS activation could uncouple ERK from PI3K-alpha inhibition and reduce drug sensitivity `pmid-28382169`.
evidence_summary: BYL719 inhibited AKT and ERK phosphorylation in PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer cells; EGFR or RAS hyperactivation and RTK inputs including EGFR, c-MET, FGFR, and HER3 restored ERK phosphorylation and cell viability, and cell-line/PDX profiling linked RTK expression with sensitivity.
reviewer_notes: The paper uses BYL719 and preclinical profiling; clinical predictive use remains proposed.

claim_text: RTK-dependent SHP2 signaling similarly reactivated ERK and PI3K outputs after alpelisib in luminal and triple-negative breast cancer models, with SHP2 blockade restoring growth control in cells, organoids, and xenografts `pmid-35365185`.
evidence_summary: Luminal/TNBC models treated with BYL719 showed RTK/growth-factor-mediated resistance with rebound ERK, AKT, S6, and 4E-BP1 signaling; SHP099 or SHP2 knockout reduced colony formation and pathway rebound, and BYL719/SHP099 blocked patient-derived organoid formation and HCC1806 xenograft growth.

claim_text: Finally, CD44-HA signaling provides a noncanonical breast cancer example in which acquired alpelisib resistance used Src-ERK-Ezrin signaling to maintain AKT-mTOR activity `pmid-33024087`.
evidence_summary: Luminal breast cancer models acquired a CD44-high state during BYL719 resistance; CD44 interaction with hyaluronan activated Src-ERK signaling and Ezrin-linked networks, maintaining AKT/mTOR activity under PI3K-alpha inhibition and restoring sensitivity when CD44/HA signaling was disrupted.
reviewer_notes: Paper frames this as adaptive/acquired resistance in luminal breast cancer models.
